Construct a 14’ wide trail parallel to Pearl Street and under the Ben Franklin Bridge.

This section of trail has been constructed as a part of the former Camden Prison site
redevelopment project.

Continue the Delaware River Promenade up to Front Street in conjunction with future
redevelopment. Exact route of trail will depend on layout of potential development.

Construct a minimum 14’ wide trail between Front Street and State Street. This trail will likely
be part of a new string of parks and environmental enhancements along the riverfront per the
North Camden Neighborhood Plan. A portion of the trail is built (but currently close to the public)
between Erie Street and State Street, but will require widening.

Convert the intersection of State Street and 10th Street to a 3-way stop. Enhance the junction of
the trail with the old State Street Bridge into a neighborhood plaza that provides placemaking,
shade, and seating.

Investigate a 3-way stop here. This intersection is the junction of the CCCT,
State Street bike lanes, old State Street bridge, and East Coast Greenway,
so many multi-modal turns will be made here.

Explore opportunities to make direct connection to Ben Franklin Bridge from here for the
convenience of daily commuters (via Elm or Pearl Streets, see map of Segment 1).

Trail routes under Conrail/RiverLine road bridge. Barrier will be needed between trail and exit
ramp. Landscaping is recommended to help visually screen the highway.

Modify deck on existing bridge over US 30 by narrowing the existing 3 vehicular lanes to 11’
wide each. Remove the guardrail and current sidewalk on the east side of the bridge, and
reconstruct a new 12’ wide trail. Install new barrier between widened sidewalk and narrowed
travel lanes.
Utilize existing trail here; no new construction necessary.

Modify Baird Blvd. intersection to create all-way stop for trail crossing. Create safe bicycle and
pedestrian access to trail on south side of Cooper River. See illustration below.
Utilize existing trail here; no new construction necessary.

Investigate a 3-way stop here. The intersection is the junction of the CCCT,

so many multi-modal turns will be made here.

Create an all-way stop and trail crossing by removing southern slip lanes
(see illustration on map).
Utilize existing trail here; no new construction necessary.

Add a crosswalk and pedestrian signals to south side of intersection; modify signal timing to
accommodate trail. Construct new curb ramps to accommodate the full width of the trail. Create
a raised crosswalk in the southeast corner slip lane for increased safety. Make a direct,intuitive
connection to the through trail with a 150’ connection from the southeast corner of the
intersection. Over the long term, a grade separated crossing here should be investigated.
Utilize existing trail here with noted enhancements.

Add 500’ of cast in place Jersey barrier to the edge of the existing sidepath on this bridge to
create a separation between traffic and trail users.

Stripe centerline of trail through this area to clearly delineate to users in both direction the
through trail that should be used.

Consider crosswalk to Pacific Avenue to create direct on-street route to Ferry Avenue PATCO

Add ramp to access Cooper River Trail from Browning Road. Make Browning Road & S. Park
Drive intersection an all-way stop with crosswalks.

Add a crosswalk and pedestrian signals to southern leg of
intersection. Conduct a traffic study to determine new signal phasing
and timing. Create a raised crosswalk at southeastern slip lane.

Add ramp to access Cooper River Trail from Browning Road. Make Browning Road & S. Park

Modify the Browning Road street section, with the goal of placing a minimum 11’ wide trail in

Current underpass at PATCO line is sufficiently wide for street and trail.
Maple Avenue approach to remain a stop.
Consider extending trail along Browning Road to Newton Lake Park Trail.

Modify the Collings Avenue street section, with the goal of placing a minimum 12’ wide trail in

Narrow Newton Avenue to 24’ wide minimum between Holly Avenue and Cedar Avenue to
